lost.label: Apologia (Uraniborg 1591; printing disputed)
lost.attested_by: Attested only by Erasmus Bartholin's first-person claim to own a printed copy 'Uraniburgi 1591' (De cometis, 1665, p.49) and by the Berlin manuscript fragment apparently copied from a print; Friis, Dreyer and Nielsen judge the imprint a bibliographic ghost.

lost.label: Apologia (Wandsbeck/Hamburg 1598)
lost.attested_by: Attested by Tycho's letter to Scultetus of 7 January 1600; no copy and no manuscript of this reissue located.

lost.label: Carmen ad Falk Gjøe (Uraniborg 1584)
lost.attested_by: Attested by Rothmann's letter of 21 September 1587 and Tycho's reply of 17 August 1588 (Epistolae astronomicae); no copy survives and the text is essentially lost.

lost.label: Carmen ad Erik Lange (Uraniborg 1584)
lost.attested_by: Attested by Tycho's own reference in the Ulfeldt poem (Nielsen §426); no copy survives — the text is preserved in Dreyer's Opera Omnia.

lost.label: Elegy to Ptolemy (conjectured Uraniborg print, 1584)
lost.attested_by: The 1584 Uraniborg broadsheet is conjectural (Brøndsted, Fund og Forskning 9, 1962): the poem, dated 1 October 1584, survives only through Frobenius's 1644 Almagest proof-sheet at the Royal Library, Stockholm.

lost.label: Elegy on Hans Frandsen (Uraniborg 1584?)
lost.attested_by: No Uraniborg print survives; the text is preserved through the reprints in Gassendi (1655) and Resen (1668).

Berlin, Gymnasium zum Grauen Kloster (Rollenhagen copy) — destroyed WW2
lost.attested_by: Recorded in Norlind's 1933 census: a presentation copy with Tycho's autograph dedication (1598) to Georg Rollenhagen; the Gymnasium's library was destroyed in the Second World War.

lost.label: Fair-copy yearly series (the apographa)
lost.attested_by: Nineteen of the twenty yearly fair-copies survive at the ÖNB, Vienna (Cod. 10657–10675); the 1593 volume was lost before Kepler's death in 1630 (Dreyer, TBOO X prolegomena).

lost.label: Lost 8vo observation volume 1563–74
lost.attested_by: On Erasmus Bartholin's receipt of 20 June 1664; seen in La Hire's rooms in Paris on 4 May 1697 (Rostgaard's letter); returned to Copenhagen 1707; borrowed by Christian Hvass in 1778 and never returned; last documented at Passy, near Paris, in 1804.

lost.label: Urania Titani — fair copy signed by Sophie Brahe, intended for Erik Lange
lost.note: The poem was designed as a verse letter in Sophie's voice to Erik Lange in Germany, and was presumably intended to be dispatched to him in a fair copy signed by Sophie herself (the epistolary fiction requires it). Zeeberg (1994) establishes the intended recipient and the epistolary frame from internal evidence. No evidence it was ever dispatched or received; untraced.
lost.attested_by: Inferred from the poem's epistolary frame — a verse letter in Sophie's voice to Erik Lange, presumably to be dispatched in a fair copy signed by her (Zeeberg 1994); no evidence of dispatch or receipt.

lost.label: Urania Titani — the written exemplar (forlæg) for Cod. Vindob. 10686/12
lost.note: The Vienna manuscript V (Cod. Vindob. Lat. 10686/12, item 12) is a scribal copy — not the original composition draft. The existence of an earlier exemplar (forlæg) is inferred from scribal transposition errors in V that are correctable to sense. Tycho's autograph corrections in V (hand T) presuppose a copy he was correcting against, which may be this forlæg or an author's working draft. Location unknown; may not have left Hven.
lost.attested_by: Inferred from scribal transposition errors in Cod. Vindob. 10686/12 and from Tycho's autograph corrections there, which presuppose an exemplar he corrected against (Zeeberg 1994).

lost.label: Radius astronomicus (cross-staff) — the student instrument
lost.attested_by: Tycho's own account of his student years, appended to the Mechanica (1598): a wooden radius he had made in 1564 after Gemma Frisius's design (trans. Raeder, Strömgren & Strömgren 1946).

lost.label: Quadrans maximus — the great Augsburg quadrant
lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in the Mechanica (1598), including Tycho's own note of its construction in Paul Hainzel's garden near Augsburg and its destruction in the December 1574 storm (trans. Raeder, Strömgren & Strömgren 1946, p.89).

lost.label: Quadrans muralis sive Tichonicus — the great mural quadrant
lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in the Mechanica (1598) — the engraving that also records the mural portrait painted within its arc.

lost.label: Brass azimuthal quadrant
lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in Tycho's Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek 1598).

lost.label: Revolving quadrant (quadrans azimuthalis volubilis)
lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in Tycho's Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek 1598).

lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in Tycho's Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek 1598).

lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in Tycho's Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek 1598).

lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in Tycho's Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek 1598).

lost.label: Triangular sextant (sextans trigonicus)
lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in Tycho's Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek 1598).

lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in Tycho's Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek 1598).

lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in Tycho's Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek 1598).

lost.label: Arcus bipartitus — the bipartite arc (1583)
lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in Tycho's Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek 1598).

lost.label: Parallactic instrument (triquetrum / regulae)
lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in Tycho's Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek 1598).

lost.label: Copernicus's triquetrum — the relic from Frauenburg
lost.attested_by: Described in the Mechanica (1598); Tycho's commemorative poem on receiving the relic from Frauenburg is printed in TBOO V, 44–47.

lost.label: Globus magnus orichalcicus — the great brass globe
lost.attested_by: Described and depicted in the Mechanica (1598); its destruction in the Copenhagen observatory-tower fire of 1728 is documented (Dreyer, Tycho Brahe, 1890).

lost.label: Horologia — the observatory clocks
lost.attested_by: Described in the Mechanica (1598; trans. Raeder, Strömgren & Strömgren 1946, p.30 — four clocks, the largest with a brass wheel of 1,200 teeth).

lost.label: The alchemical laboratory
lost.attested_by: Described in Tycho's own published account of Uraniborg (Mechanica, 1598) — the basement laboratory with its sixteen furnaces — and in visitors' reports (Christianson, On Tycho's Island, 2000).

lost.label: The library and the great globe
lost.attested_by: Described in Tycho's own published account of Uraniborg (Mechanica, 1598), which places the great brass globe in the library (Dreyer 1890).

lost.label: The printing house (Tycho's press)
lost.attested_by: Attested by the surviving Uraniborg imprints themselves and by Tycho's correspondence; documented in Nielsen, Tyge Brahes Bogtrykkeri paa Hveen (1921).

lost.label: The paper mill
lost.attested_by: Attested in royal chancery records — the rag-privilege of 2 March 1592 and the demolition order of 26 June 1602 (Kancelliets Brevbøger) — and in Tycho's correspondence with Hájek; the site was excavated 1933–34.

lost.label: The Curtius (Kurtz) house — Tycho's Prague residence and place of death
lost.attested_by: Described in Tycho's own letters from Prague; contemporary records place his death there on 24 October 1601 (Dreyer 1890; Thoren, The Lord of Uraniborg, 1990).

lost.label: The mural quadrant portrait (Uraniborg)
lost.attested_by: Known from Tycho's own description and the engraving of the great mural quadrant in the Mechanica (1598), which reproduce the painted scene; the painting itself was lost with Uraniborg.

lost.label: Justus Lipsius, De constantia
lost.attested_by: A lost Danish-collection Tychonianum: Tycho's copy carried his own critical remarks dated 1592 on the first leaf; formerly in the University Library, Copenhagen (Jens Kragh Hoest, Chronos 1822, p.24); now lost.

lost.label: Niels Krag, Republica Lacedaemoniorum (1593) — copy with Tycho's autograph distichs
lost.attested_by: A lost Danish-collection Tychonianum with Tycho's autograph distichs. The extant Copenhagen University Library copy is not Tycho's: it is the author's dedication copy to Jacob Ulfeldt. Tycho's copy (ex-Rostgaard) is lost.

lost.label: Detached signature 'd:Dt: Tÿcho Brahe' (ex Lynge; excised from an Uraniborg imprint) — ILAB Missing Books 2015
lost.attested_by: From the stock of Herman H.J. Lynge & Søn, Copenhagen (catalogue item 36189); reported missing in the ILAB Missing Books Register, 22 January 2015.
